subject: subset or extract from a methylbase object

messages.author: b5b1db21b60ddd4a
messages.subject: subset or extract from a methylbase object
parts:
Dear all,

 

I want to analyse a smaller set of CGs from my methylbase files instead of all of them.

 

I have a list of CG coordinates in a data frame (df) with column information for chr, start, end and strand and I  want to extract these specific rows from my methylbase object (meth2), where the output remains as a methylbase object.

 

I have seen the following:

subset2=meth2[1:100,]

but this seems to work only for specific lines.  I want the [1:100] part to somehow point to the file “df” and the subset2 to be a class of methylbase.

 

How can one do this?

 

Michelle

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: subset or extract from a methylbase object
parts:
I've had to solve a similar problem- see below for my solution modified for your situation. I think (hope?) there's a more efficient way, but this will get the job done. The basic idea is that we create a list and query by pasting all the position info together, and check for inclusion with the %in% operator.

getSites<-function(query.df, meth.base){
      dat=getData(meth.base)[ , c('chr', 'start','strand')]
      base.pos=paste(dat$chr, dat$start, dat$strand , sep='.' )
      
      query.pos=paste(query.df$chr, query.df$start, query.df$strand , sep='.' )

      return_indices=(1:(dim(dat)[[1]]))[ base.pos %in% query.pos ]
      output=select(meth.base, return_indices)

 }

Hi Piotr,

Since this question was posted there were a lot updates done to the package, so maybe you can have a look at the latest vignette: 
https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#53_selection:_subsetting_methylkit_objects

I think the function selectByOverlap could be of interest for you, especially if you have a data frame (df) with column information for chr, start, end and strand. Then you can basically use it like this:

library(methylKit)

df <- data.frame(chr = "chr21", 
                 start = c(9853296,9853326,9860126),
                 end = c(9853296,9853326,9860126))

gr <- makeGRangesFromDataFrame(df)

selectByOverlap(methylBase.obj,gr)

Best,
Alex
